evidence_gaps_add: No independent comparison found that prints per-method rejection of unseen cell types (unknown-population F1 or AUROC) for CellTypist, scANVI, SingleR, Azimuth or scArches; such results appear in developer method papers or in figures.
Wu et al. 2025's novel-cell-type results (AUROC and AUPRC across unseen ratios) and its logistic regression and scVI baselines are figure-only.
Boiarsky et al. 2023 (logistic regression against scBERT and scGPT) prints its tables as images in the preprint; the published version was not retrieved.
The extracted cross-atlas transfer uses the atlases' own labels as truth (use-case exclusion) and scores only the 14 shared cell types.

summary_proposal.source_locator: cell-type-20261009-source-wu2025-supp: Supplementary Tables S2 and S3
summary_proposal.text: When six single-cell foundation models were used to transfer labels between two public atlases (Wu et al. 2025), every model reached an Accuracy@1 above 0.6 on the 14 cell types the atlases share, but macro-F1 stayed low: 0.080 to 0.105 from Tabula Sapiens to the lung atlas (HLCA), and 0.209 to 0.283 in the other direction. The best pairwise ensembles reached 0.164 and 0.303. The truth labels are the atlases' own annotations, only shared cell types are scored, and these tables do not test whether a workflow can recognise cell types missing from the reference. Conventional baselines appear only in the paper's figures.
summary_proposal.caveat_note: The supplement source carries an evidence concern (full-ensemble text and table disagree), so the summary cannot become active until it is resolved.

gaps: Rejection of unsupported populations: no printed per-method values from an independent source.
Wu et al. 2025 intra-dataset results, the novel-type OOD results and the baselines are figure-only.
No CellTypist, scANVI, SingleR, Azimuth or scArches values in this pass.
concerns_for_reviewer: Evidence concern on the supplement source: Results 'Cross-dataset validation' paragraph 4 says logit aggregation has the higher Accuracy@1 and majority voting the higher macro-F1. Both tables print the reverse (S2: 0.758 vs 0.753 accuracy, 0.163 vs 0.119 macro-F1; S3: 0.83 vs 0.82, 0.285 vs 0.28). The extractor asserts the table direction.
Both tables print the same 15 pair labels in the same member order; configurations are keyed on the unordered pair anyway, and each evaluation keeps the printed row label in source_label.
Origin is independent_paper for all 46 evaluations: the source does not state that any author developed the evaluated models. A reviewer may want to check the author lists of LangCell and scCello.
The supplementary workbook also contains donor-level demographic metadata (Table S6, AIDA v2). It was not extracted, and the workbook is not archived (CC BY-NC-ND).
Both judgements are proxy: atlas labels as truth, shared types only, and no rejection endpoint in the tables.
